Andrew Tate By CNN Newssource July 19, 2026 5:56 PM Published July 19, 2026 4:19 PM By Holmes Lybrand, Dalia Faheid, Hannah Rabinowitz, Alea Motwane, CNN (CNN) — US Marshals arrested social media influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate in Miami Saturday on an extradition request from the United Kingdom following an investigation into sexual offenses reported by seven victims, according to the UK Crown Prosecution Service. UK officials accused the brothers of abusing women in the East of England region, just north of London, between 2010 and 2017. Andrew Tate, a self-proclaimed misogynist with billions of views online, faces 42 charges, including rape, human trafficking, indecent images of a child and assault, according to the UK Crown Prosecution Service and Bedfordshire Police . Tristan Tate faces 17 charges, including sexual assault, rape and trafficking, officials said. “Officers from our major crime unit have been working closely alongside the Crown Prosecution Service and both national and international law enforcement agencies as part of this complex investigation,” Bedfordshire Assistant Chief Constable Karena Thomas said. The Department of Justice confirmed US Marshals arrested Andrew and Tristan Tate “pursuant to extradition proceedings,” adding the arrests “were made in accordance with the treaties and law enforcement agreements governing Justice Department extraditions.” The brothers will appear in Miami federal court on Monday, their attorney, Joeseph McBride, told CNN on Sunday. The brothers are expected to reject the extradition request, McBride added. The brothers are innocent, McBride said and criticized the UK’s move to seek extradition. “There is a long-standing agreement between the UK and Romanian governments that the UK would not seek extradition while the Romanian proceedings are pending,” McBride said. “Those proceedings are ongoing right now. That agreement exists because no nation gets to trample the judicial sovereignty of another for political convenience.” In a statement posted to X Sunday, McBride said the brothers were arrested for their politics and are being held in solitary confinement. The brothers were in Washington, DC, earlier this month where they held political meetings, McBride told CNN. CNN has reached out to Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier for information about where and how the brothers are being held. Romanian prosecutors previously accused the brothers of trafficking women across Romania, the United Kingdom and the US and sexually exploiting them. The Tates have repeatedly rejected the allegations made against them in that case. CNN has reached out to Romania’s justice ministry for comment on their arrest. Advocates have warned against the pair’s rising tide of influence among young boys and men. Andrew Tate is known for his aggressive speech about male dominance, female submission and wealth. At one point, he was suspended from major social media platforms. The brothers, who have dual American and British citizenship, face dozens of new charges added onto previous charges brought by the Crown Prosecution Service after evidence was submitted by Bedfordshire Police, authorities said. The new charges were brought after officials had investigated reports made by four additional victims in the East England areas of Bedfordshire and Hertfordshire, police said. Andrew Tate is also facing a civil suit in the UK, which is being brought by four women who accuse the social media influencer of rape. A spokesperson for Tate previously told CNN that their client “categorically denies these unproven and untested allegations.” Matthew Jury, an attorney representing the four women, welcomed Tate’s arrest. “We do not yet know whether these new charges relate to the complaints made by my clients or by other women,” Jury said in a statement Sunday. “But any step that advances the proper administration of justice deserves to be welcomed.” The brothers left Romania after Romanian authorities lifted travel restrictions on them, arriving in Florida in February 2025. Upon their arrival, they found themselves at the heart of another criminal investigation — when Attorney General Uthmeier announced the probe, led by the Office of Statewide Prosecution. They had taken aim at Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis, who previously suggested they were not welcome in his state. “When Americans who are unfairly imprisoned abroad return home you betray them,” Andrew Tate said on X last year. “You better nail me now. Let’s go. Arrest me.” Thomas, the Bedfordshire Police official, said “there is no place for male violence against women and girls.” “We will continue to work tirelessly to support victims and investigate all reports made to us,” Thomas said. This story has been updated with additional information. The-CNN-Wire ™ & © 2026 Cable News Network, Inc., a Warner Bros. Discovery Company. All rights reserved. CNN’s Amanda Musa contributed to this report. https://www.dw.com/en/hungary-s-parliame.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5Ie3x Andras Baka was ousted by Orban as head of the Supreme Court in 2011, but now replaces a president whose term was cut short by Orban's successor Image: Bernadett Szabo/REUTERS Advertisement Hungary 's parliament voted in Andras Baka, formerly the head of the Supreme Court, as the country's next president on Tuesday. The symbolic step is part of new Prime Minister Peter Magyar's sweeping efforts to dismantle the legacy of former premier Viktor Orban after winning April's general elections . Baka was a staunch critic of Orban who was removed from his Supreme Court role during the former PM's tenure. Now, he will replace Tamas Sulyok, a president appointed by Orban , whose term in office was shortened via constitutional amendment in order to remove him from the largely ceremonial role. What happened in Tuesday's parliamentary vote? The vote in parliament to appoint Baka was always likely to be a formality, given the massive majority that Magyar's conservative, pro-European TISZA party holds in the chamber. It went almost entirely along party lines, 140 lawmakers voted in favor and six voted against. TISZA holds 141 seats. Orban's right-wing populist Fidesz party, which has 52 lawmakers, boycotted the vote in protest — but did so knowing it would be powerless to prevent Baka's appointment. Baka took his oath of office and gave a short speech to the chamber after Tuesday's vote Image: Bernadett Szabo/REUTERS Who is Andras Baka? Baka, 73, is a jurist and politician who was briefly a member of parliament from 1990 to 1991. He spent almost 20 years as a judge at the European Court of Human Rights (ECHR), before returning to Hungary in 2009 to become president of its Supreme Court. In December 2011, not long after Orban returned to power as prime minister after a stint in opposition, he was removed from his role three years before his term was set to expire and sidelined from public life in Hungary. Magyar said Baka's life served "as an example of commitment to the democratic rule of law and constitutional principles" as the central European country needs to be "guided back onto the path of the rule of law and constitutional governance." Baka, 73, spent almost 20 years at the European Court of Human Rights earlier in his career as a jurist Image: Zoltan Balogh/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance Why was Baka's appointment and his predecessor's removal contentious? Baka's appointment prompted protests from Fidesz, but also some critical comments elsewhere in Hungary, with some rights watchdogs likening the removal of Tamas Sulyok to the "illiberal" practices of the Orban-era. Sulyok, appointed in 2024, was deemed an Orban ally. Magyar used his two-thirds majority in parliament — which he holds thanks to Hungary's winner-takes-all first-past-the-post electoral system, as Orban used to — to amend the constitution and bring his term to an early end. Fidesz and their nationalist KDNP allies in parliament had called this " tyrannical " and "illegitimate," while Magyar argued it was necessary to pursue the "system change" he promised amid April's landslide election victory. Magyar briefly tapped Hungarian national treasure and chess superstar Judit Polgar as a possible replacement president, but she quickly declined, saying she did not feel she had "the strength to take on the historic responsibility of uniting a divided nation," but pledging to do "everything in my power" to support a new, independent and respected president. Magyar initially floated the notion of presidential star power, until chess phenom Judit Polgar said 'thanks, but no thanks' Image: Judit Polgar Foundation What has Baka said about the process and his appointment? Baka himself had not criticized Sulyok's removal, despite the echoes of the mechanisms used to oust him in 2011. "In a country governed by the rule of law, such extraordinary measures cannot be used, but Hungary became a captured state under Orban," he told the AFP news agency last month. He said that state officials like Sulyok "were appointed not to restrain the government's power, but to ensure the political survival of the former system even after an electoral defeat." However, speaking in parliament on Tuesday, Baka seemed to strike a conciliatory tone, even for supporters of the old regime. "There is one thing we certainly cannot do: we cannot build the new Hungary on revenge," he told parliament, vowing to "encourage public and professional debate, uphold [parliament's] openness and impartiality, and consistently insist that constitution-making must never again become the exclusive project of a single political force." https://www.politico.eu/article/eu-to-pr.text: BRUSSELS — The EU is preparing to try and persuade Canada and the U.K. to increase their support for Ukraine as part of efforts to plug the €70 billion funding gap Kyiv faces next year. The EU-Canada summit on Oct. 29-30 and the EU-U.K. summit on Nov. 20 will give Brussels a chance to make the case at the highest level. With Kyiv’s financing needs rising and U.S. backing uncertain, Brussels is increasingly looking to non-EU allies to contribute more, five EU officials, including two from the European Commission, and two EU diplomats told POLITICO. The EU and its member countries provide 80 percent of Ukraine’s external aid, Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Friday. “We urgently need other partners to step up.” Advertisement Advertisement The EU has committed to a €90 billion loan for 2026 and 2027, intended to cover about two-thirds of Ukraine’s needs. Brussels had expected other partners — including Canada, Japan, South Korea, Australia and Norway — to provide another €45 billion, but much of that money has been slow to arrive as other governments have yet to firm up or disburse the support Brussels expected. While calls to help Ukraine defend itself are not new, the projected 2027 bill has grown as Russia intensifies its assault, the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran drives up costs and Washington shifts toward positions more favorable to Moscow — leaving Europe and other allies to shoulder more of the cost of keeping Kyiv afloat. Brussels is heading into negotiations about closer economic and defense ties with London and Ottawa. Diplomats and EU officials said they do not expect a formal bargain, but that support for Kyiv from the EU’s partners is likely to shape the political climate around the talks. Like others in this article, they were granted anonymity to speak about the sensitive diplomacy. European Council President Antonio Costa, Ukraine president Volodymyr Zelenskyy and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen at the European Council Summit in Brussels on Oct. 16. | Nicolas Maeterlinck/Belga/AFP via Getty Images The EU has also raised Ukraine’s 2027 financing needs at meetings of the International Monetary Fund, the G7 and the G20, as well as with Gulf Cooperation Council countries. “During my meetings in Bangkok, the need to secure financial support for Ukraine in 2027 was a prominent topic,” European Economy Commissioner Valdis Dombrovskis told POLITICO, referencing last week’s IMF and World Bank Group meetings. He said he called for “broad burden sharing and stressed the importance of international partners each doing their part as Ukraine continues fighting Russian aggression.” All the EU officials and diplomats stressed that the push was not a criticism of the U.K. or Canada, both of which are strong supporters of Ukraine. The point, they said, is that Kyiv’s needs have grown. Advertisement Advertisement The U.K. says it has committed a total of £25 billion for Ukraine and Canada has promised the equivalent of €5.4 billion in military assistance and €8.2 billion in direct financial support. The EU and its member countries say they have contributed over €231 billion since Russia’s full-scale invasion, including military aid, budget support and guarantees, support for Ukrainians hosted in the bloc, and proceeds from immobilized Russian assets — an amount one senior EU diplomat described as already “over and above.” How to meet Ukraine’s financial needs has become “a central discussion in every single meeting” with partners supporting Kyiv, a Commission official said. The push to secure Ukraine’s financial needs comes as support for Kyiv will be tested in a series of elections across Europe next year. In France, far-right front-runner Marine Le Pen has vowed to end aid if elected president in 2027, while in Italy, Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni faces a challenge from Russia-friendly Roberto Vannacci ahead of next year’s election. The looming votes, combined with the unpredictability of Washington’s backing for Kyiv, mean European countries need to look beyond their own budgets, the senior diplomat said. “We need to think wider and broader.” The EU is also urging the Ukrainian government to secure more support from non-EU backers. “This is the first next step that they need to secure from their partners,” the Commission official said. Advertisement Advertisement Not ‘pulling a Trump’ EU ambassadors are set to talk about the upcoming Canada and U.K. summits tomorrow, with Ukraine funding expected to form part of the discussions, the two diplomats said. Brussels, “without pointing the finger,” wants to use the run-up to the meetings to press for broader support, the senior diplomat said. But the EU “won’t be pulling a Trump” and explicitly linking favorable treatment to contributions to Ukraine, they added. The Commission has not set out what it will ask partners for or how any request might connect to trade and defense talks. The diplomat said the EU still needed to work out “how much will translate in joining those dots.” Ukraine’s Foreign Affairs Minister Andrii Sybiha greets British Prime Minister Andy Burnham upon his arrival by train in Kyiv for indepence commemorations on Aug. 24. | Henry Nicholls/WPA Pool/Getty Images Von der Leyen proposed making Canada the EU’s first “associate member” in her State of the Union speech last month. The October summit in Montreal is an opportunity to develop the idea. Ottawa will participate in the EU’s SAFE program, which finances joint defense procurement, giving Canadian companies preferential access to SAFE-funded contracts. Closer defense cooperation and industrial access could form part of the wider conversation about support for Kyiv, one of the diplomats said. In a statement to POLITICO, Kathryn Serieux, a spokesperson for Canada’s Privy Council Office, said Ottawa “is and has been a steadfast supporter of Ukraine,” with Canada committing nearly C$26 billion in military, financial development and humanitarian assistance. Advertisement Advertisement “Canada continues to stand by Ukraine and remains engaged with international partners on Ukraine’s needs,” Serieux said. The U.K. summit is expected to advance Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s promised reset with the bloc, including agreements on youth mobility, food and emissions trading. Burnham has said the status quo is “not good enough” and wants Britain to move closer to the EU. London wants U.K. companies to count as European under the proposed Industrial Accelerator Act, which would give preference to goods made in Europe in public contracts and industrial support. British officials worry U.K. firms could lose out despite close links between British and European supply chains. Three U.K. officials said Tuesday they had not heard of a request for Britain to provide more support for Ukraine in exchange for letting its companies qualify under the act. A fourth EU official said Ukraine was expected to feature in the summit declaration with the U.K., but that it would reflect both sides’ efforts to help Kyiv, rather than a Brussels demand for more support. The EU is also pressing Japan to increase its contributions, with one senior EU official saying it was lagging in 2026. A person familiar with the thinking in Tokyo pushed back on the idea that Japan was not pulling its weight, saying Tokyo had already given around $20 billion in support to Kyiv — but there could be room for more if Ukraine requested it. Tokyo is also seeking assurances that Japanese companies will retain access to the EU market, following concerns the Industrial Accelerator Act’s “Made in Europe” preferences could put its firms at a disadvantage. Advertisement Advertisement The Mission of Japan to the EU didn’t respond to a request for comment. Australia says it has not yet received a request for more funding for Ukraine for 2027. Canberra is likely lower on the list, if it is on it at all, because its prime minister and foreign minister met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy at the U.N. General Assembly last month and announced additional funding and a security agreement, an Australian official said. Dan Bloom contributed reporting from London. Amanda Copp contributed reporting from Canberra. Mike Blanchfield contributed reporting from Ottawa.

Please review their details and accept them to load the content. Manage Preferences Polish prosecutors have charged a 66-year-old man with planning to overthrow the government by force. Krzysztof N. has been charged with nine offences, including planning to overthrow Poland's state authorities, including the prime minister and the Council of Ministers, by force using explosives he had collected, an offence punishable by two to 15 years in prison. The remaining charges concern online recordings and posts allegedly promoting the violent seizure of power, violence to achieve political change, war of aggression in Ukraine, and crimes motivated by nationality, ethnicity, race or political affiliation. The man was detained on Sunday. A search of his home uncovered more than a dozen items initially identified as improvised explosive devices, some resembling fragmentation grenades. Officers also found objects resembling firearms, initially classified as alarm weapons or pneumatic weapons, a list of people who had been in contact with the suspect, and computer equipment. Digital material has been sent for analysis. Online material reportedly indicated the creation of an extremist group promoting the violent seizure of power. The suspect said it was to consist of three units, with a fourth being formed. Many Facebook posts and videos were removed shortly after his arrest. He has denied the charges and refused to give an explanation. He said he did not understand the alleged offences and referred to physical and mental health conditions. He may provide a statement later after consulting a lawyer. Prosecutor Piotr Antoni Skiba said there was currently no indication that the group had been inspired by foreign intelligence services, although investigators were examining this possibility. Proceedings concerning various online posts promoting behaviour contrary to the law had been conducted by the Kielce Regional Prosecutor's Office in recent weeks and were transferred to prosecutors in Warsaw on Tuesday. On Sunday, Poland's Interior Ministry said police had received information about a possible attack targeting Prime Minister Donald Tusk and Deputy Prime Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz. A meeting involving police, the State Protection Service and the Internal Security Agency was convened at the Internal Security Agency's Counterterrorism Centre before the suspect was detained that afternoon.
